title: Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 — Member Rights & Governance
content:
The Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002 governs cooperative societies whose objects and activities extend to more than one state in India, replacing the 1984 Act.

Membership rights: Every member of a multi-state cooperative society has the right to attend and vote at general meetings, the right to receive a copy of the annual report and audited accounts, the right to inspect the society's books of account and other records at reasonable times, and the right to stand for election to the board of directors subject to the society's bye-laws. A member cannot be expelled from the society except by a resolution passed at a general meeting by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, and only after being given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

Board of directors: The board manages the affairs of the society in accordance with the Act, rules and bye-laws. The maximum number of directors on the board is 21, and the term of office of an elected director is 5 years from the date of election, unless the bye-laws provide otherwise. At least two seats on the board must be reserved for women members, and at least one seat for members belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, where such members exist.

General body meetings: Every multi-state cooperative society must hold its annual general meeting within six months of the close of the financial year. Notice of not less than 14 days must be given to every member for a general meeting, along with the agenda.

Audit: Every multi-state cooperative society must get its accounts audited at least once a year by an auditor from a panel approved by the Central Registrar. The audit report must be placed before the general body.

Dissolution and surcharge: The Central Registrar may order an inquiry into the affairs of a society, and if a director or officer is found to have caused loss to the society through negligence or misconduct, the Registrar may order that person to make good the loss (surcharge proceedings).

Grievances against a multi-state cooperative society, including disputes about membership, elections or management, may be referred to the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies or, for disputes between members and the society, resolved through arbitration under the Act's dispute-resolution provisions before approaching civil courts.
